chunks: And by this chain, from Ṣāliḥ ibn ʿUqbah, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) said to Fāṭimah (عليها السلام): “O Fāṭimah, arise and bring out that dish.” So she arose and brought out a dish in which there was tharīd and boiling meat broth. Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn ate from it for thirteen days.

Then Umm Ayman saw al-Ḥusayn with something, so she said to him: “From where do you have this?” He said: “We have been eating it for days.” Then Umm Ayman came to Fāṭimah and said: “O Fāṭimah, when there is something with Umm Ayman, it is for Fāṭimah and her children; but when there is something with Fāṭimah, is there to be nothing from it for Umm Ayman?”

So she brought some of it out for her, and Umm Ayman ate from it, and the dish was exhausted. Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) said to her: “Had you not fed her from it, you and your offspring would have continued to eat from it until the Hour is established.” Then Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “And the dish is with us; our Qāʾim (عليه السلام) will come forth with it in his time.”

key_terms.السَّاعَةُ: the Hour, meaning the final establishment of Qiyamah
key_terms.الصَّحْفَةَ: the dish or tray from which the blessed food was eaten
key_terms.ثَرِيدٌ: crumbled bread mixed with broth; a prepared food dish
key_terms.عُرَاقٌ: meat broth or gravy accompanying the food
key_terms.قَائِمُنَا: our Qāʾim, the divinely guided one who will arise

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of the blessed dish of Fāṭimah (عليها السلام) in al-Kāfī say?
ai.summary: This narration describes a blessed dish from which the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله), Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī, Fāṭimah, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn (عليهم السلام) ate for many days. It also highlights Umm Ayman’s closeness to the Ahl al-Bayt and concludes with a statement from Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) that the dish remains with them and will appear with the Qāʾim (عليه السلام).

en.hubeali:
And by this chain, from Salih Bin Uqba, from Amro Bin Shimr, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to (Syeda) Fatima<sup>asws</sup>: ‘O Fatima<sup>asws</sup>! Arise and bring out that tray to me<sup>saww</sup>’.

So she<sup>asws</sup> arose and brought out a tray which contained porridge and some steamed meat. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and Ali<sup>asws</sup>, and (Syed) Fatima<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> ate (from it) for thirteen days.

Then Umm Ayman<sup>as</sup> saw Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> having something with him<sup>asws</sup>, so she<sup>as</sup> said to him<sup>asws</sup>: ‘From where did this come for you<sup>asws</sup>?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup> have been eating it for days’. So Umm Ayman<sup>as</sup> came over to (Syeda) Fatima<sup>asws</sup> and she<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Fatima<sup>asws</sup>! Whenever there is something for Umm Ayman<sup>as</sup>, so rather it would be for (Syeda) Fatima<sup>asws</sup> and her<sup>asws</sup> children, and when there was something with (Syeda) Fatima<sup>asws</sup>, so there isn’t anything from it for Umm Ayman<sup>as</sup>?’

So she<sup>asws</sup> brought out for her<sup>as</sup>, from it, and Umm Ayman<sup>as</sup> ate from it and the tray ran out. So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said to her<sup>asws</sup>: ‘But, had you<sup>asws</sup> not fed her<sup>as</sup>, there would have eaten from it, yourself<sup>asws</sup> and your<sup>asws</sup> offspring, until the Establishment of the Hour’. 
Then Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And the tray is with us<sup>asws</sup>. Our<sup>asws</sup> Qaim<sup>asws</sup> would come out with it during his<sup>asws</sup> era’.
en.sarwar: 6. Through the same chain of narrators it is narrated from Salih ibn ‘Aqaba from Yazid ibn ‘Abd al-Malik from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following.
“When Fatima (a.s.) was born Allah sent an angel to make the tongue of Muhammad (s.a) call her ‘Fatima’. Then he said, “I set you free (from ignorance) with knowledge and set you free from menses.”
Abu Ja‘far (a.s.) then said, “By Allah, He had set her free with knowledge (from ignorance) and from menses at the time universal covenant (al-Mithaq).”
